headline: Indian benchmark indices remain under pressure amid global headwinds, crude volatility, and foreign fund outflows.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Persistent foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows drag down market sentiment.
Concerns over elevated crude oil prices and global rate hikes weigh on equities.
Global macroeconomic headwinds and weakness in foreign markets spill over into domestic indices.
Sensex and Nifty ended September recording one of their worst monthly and nine-month performances.
whatHappening: Indian benchmark indices logged their worst monthly performance since March following sustained capital outflows.
Indian rupee rebounded to 95.83 against the US dollar as crude prices showed signs of easing.
The central government reduced export duties on diesel and aviation turbine fuel while keeping petrol unchanged.
Aurobindo Pharma's subsidiary Acrotech entered the US dermatology market through the launch of Adquey.
summary:
Indian equities ended September on a weak note due to foreign portfolio outflows, global rate hike fears, and crude oil volatility.
Government interventions included slashing export duties on diesel and ATF, while the rupee showed a slight recovery against the US dollar.
Individual corporate developments saw Aurobindo Pharma expand its footprint in the US dermatology sector via its subsidiary Acrotech.
